title: bonus — add lighting (Lambertian)

atoms.evidence: same Moller-Trumbore matrix+inside-test as 0_1_6/8; still the geometric backbone
same double-repeat for (NR, NT) batch as 0_1_6/8
t.stack([-D, B - A, C - A], dim=-1) for the 3x3 system
s[~intersects] = float('inf') — needed for the s.min(dim=-1) call to skip non-hits
triangles.to(device), rays.to(device), light.to(device), and .cpu() return; device-aware throughout
t.eye(3).to(device); light.to(device) — both inline helpers moved to match GPU operands
normals = t.cross(triangles[:, 2] - triangles[:, 0], triangles[:, 1] - triangles[:, 0], dim=1) — surface normals via cross-product; help dropdown teaches this directly
normals /= normals.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True) — unit-normalize batch of normals; keepdim preserves broadcast
einops.einsum(normals, light.to(device), 'nt dims, dims -> nt') — dot product of each normal with the light vector via einsum

t.where(intensity_per_triangle > 0, intensity_per_triangle, 0.0) — clip backward-facing normals to zero; AND a second t.where(closest_distances.isfinite(), intensity, 0.0) for no-hit pixels; help dropdown teaches both
intensity_per_triangle_signed[closest_triangles_for_each_ray] — gather per-ray intensity from per-triangle intensity via int-tensor indices returned by s.min(dim=-1)

atoms_in_seed_but_not_actually_present.reason: 0_1_6 used einops.reduce(s, 'NR NT -> NR', 'min'); this exercise switched to s.min(dim=-1) because it needs BOTH the values and indices (the indices feed index-by-tensor for per-ray triangle lookup). The semantically-similar atom is different: it's torch.Tensor.min returning (vals, idx), not a reduce

notes: 14 atoms — by far the densest exercise of part1, as expected for a 5-star bonus that composes essentially every atom in the vocab. The genuine new content is the lighting computation: cross-product-normal + vector-normalize-keepdim + einsum-contraction + where-clip-negative + index-by-tensor. The switch from einops.reduce to s.min(dim=-1) is structurally important — the exercise needs gather indices to look up per-triangle intensity by closest triangle. Possible NEW atom: 'tensor-min-with-indices' (Tensor.min(dim) returns (vals, idx) — qualitatively different from a pure reduce). Not promoting yet; flag for cross-chapter recurrence (attention argmax, top-k will revisit). cuda-empty-cache only fires in the driver loop (not in lambert function body), so I omitted it here.
